title: The invention of the weekend
text: {{1}} was the factories of the industrial north {{2}} first needed the two-day break: six-day weeks left machinery idle on Sunday, {{3}} the new leisure industries wanted customers with time to spend. {{4}} the 1930s, however, Saturday remained a full working day for most. Henry Ford adopted the five-day week in 1926, {{5}} other employers dismissed as indulgence until they found their rested workers {{6}} productive than their exhausted ones. Once workers had tasted the free weekend, they organised to defend it, {{7}} by the middle of the century the two days had spread from factory to office to school. {{8}} is a curious thought that an institution as beloved as the weekend began life as an industrial efficiency measure.
